note: Event cards typed by Orbis from the cited Wikipedia articles. Dates are stored in the Gregorian calendar; cards marked Julian also show the date as their sources give it.

items.title: Defenestration of Prague
items.text: Protestant Bohemian nobles threw two imperial governors and a secretary out of a window of Prague Castle. All three survived; the revolt that followed grew into the Thirty Years' War.

items.title: Battle of White Mountain
items.text: Imperial and Catholic League troops crushed the Bohemian rebels outside Prague. Bohemia was forcibly re-Catholicised.

items.title: Sack of Magdeburg
items.text: Imperial and League troops stormed the Protestant city of Magdeburg. About 20,000 defenders and civilians died; of some 25,000 inhabitants about 5,000 survived.

items.title: Battle of Lützen
items.text: The Swedish army beat Wallenstein's imperial army near Leipzig, but King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden was killed in the battle.

items.title: Peace of Westphalia
items.text: Treaties negotiated at Münster and Osnabrück ended the war. Calvinists won the same rights as Lutherans; the princes could make alliances abroad; Sweden gained Western Pomerania, Bremen-Verden and Wismar; France kept Metz, Toul, Verdun and Habsburg rights in Alsace; the Swiss and Dutch were recognised as outside the Empire. Protestant delegates dated it 14 October.

items.title: Protestants switch calendars
items.text: The Protestant estates of the Empire adopted an 'improved calendar': Sunday 18 February 1700 was followed by Monday 1 March. For 117 years, Catholic and Protestant neighbours had dated letters ten days apart.

items.title: Gregorian calendar
items.text: Pope Gregory XIII's reform dropped ten days: Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed by Friday 15 October. Catholic states adopted it within a few years; the Empire's Protestant estates refused a calendar issued by the pope.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Gregorian calendar'; 'Adoption of the Gregorian calendar'
